baseline_and_implementation_context.text: Baselines. We adopt three navigation baselines that leverage SOTA world models: Diamond (Alonso et al., 2024) (UNet-based diffusion), NWM (Bar et al., 2025) (CDiT-based diffusion), and NWM (lang), our language-augmented variant of NWM where CLIP-encoded instructions are summed with action and time embeddings and fed through CDiT’s AdaLN block. We further include two policy-only baselines, GNM (Shah et al., 2022) (lang) and NoMaD (Sridhar et al., 2024) (lang), adapted by replacing their image-goal encoder with a frozen CLIP text encoder followed by an MLP that projects instructions into the original goal-token space. Each baseline is retrained from scratch on the LCVN training split, with LCVN-AC trained specifically for each world-model baseline. To isolate language guidance, we evaluate two ablated variants: LCVN-Uni (w/o ins), which removes instructions only from observation-prediction substep, and LCVN-WM (w/o ins), trained without language conditioning.

Datasets & Implementation Details. Experiments are conducted on our proposed LCVN dataset (Sec. 3.1) using the val seen, val unseen, and test splits. For LCVN-WM and LCVN-AC, we train an ImageVAE (Kingma and Welling, 2013) from scratch to compress images into 32\times 32 latents. LCVN-Uni is fine-tuned on GAIR Anole-7B (Chern et al., 2024) (4096-token context), while keeping the text and image tokenizers as well as the bin-token encoder frozen. Input images are resized to 448\times 448 (height \times width) and discretized into 784 visual tokens when context size is 1 or 2, and into 625 tokens when context size is 4. All models are trained on 4\timesNVIDIA A100 GPUs (80GB each). Due to space limits, kindly refer to Appendix for additional implementation details.

Diamond (Alonso et al., 2024) We select Diamond as one of the world-model baselines for comparison, as it represents a typical UNet-based diffusion world model. We adopt DIAMOND in its best configuration following the official implementation (Alonso et al., 2024). The diffusion model is trained to autoregressively predict future states at a resolution of 56×56, with an additional upsampler to generate outputs at 224×224. Continuous actions are incorporated through a linear embedding layer for conditioning. We pair Diamond with LCVN-AC to jointly support action prediction and imagination, training LCVN-AC from scratch on LCVN dataset train split, with Diamond replacing LCVN-WM as world model.

NWM (Bar et al., 2025) We select NWM as another baseline world model for comparison, as it represents a typical DiT-based diffusion architecture. For training, we adopt NWM’s best reported configuration: context length = 4, goal state = 4, and a CDiT-XL backbone with 1B parameters, training NWM from scratch on the LCVN dataset train split. For inference, we follow the settings in their paper and use 250 diffusion denoising steps to achieve optimal performance. To jointly support action prediction and imagination, we pair NWM with LCVN-AC, training LCVN-AC from scratch on LCVN dataset train split, with NWM replacing LCVN-WM as world model.

LCVN-WM For LCVN-WM, we first train an ImageVAE (Kingma and Welling, 2013) from scratch to compress input images into 32×32 latent representations. Then we build the model upon a DiT-XL backbone with approximately 1B parameters and a hidden size of 1152. Training leverages diffusion forcing (Chen et al., 2024), ensuring that each frame retains independent noise levels. We employ the AdamW optimizer (Loshchilov and Hutter, 2017) with linear warmup and a constant learning rate of 1e-4. For sampling and inference, we adopt the deterministic DDIM sampler (Song et al., 2020) with 50 steps following (Song et al., 2025).

LCVN-Uni LCVN-Uni is fine-tuned on GAIR Anole-7B (Chern et al., 2024) with a 4096-token context, while keeping the bin, text and image tokenizers frozen. Input images are resized to 448\times 448 (height \times width) and discretized into 784 visual tokens when the context size is 1 or 2, and into 625 tokens when the context size is 4. During training, only the LoRA (Hu et al., 2022) adapters (rank = 16) in the Transformer’s qkv projections are updated (Liu et al., 2023). Optimization is performed with AdamW for 20 epochs using a learning rate of 2\times 10^{-4}. Training is conducted on 4\timesNVIDIA A100 GPUs (80GB each) with a global batch size of 8 (per-GPU batch size = 1, gradient accumulation = 2).

display_rules: Render cell.raw to preserve published precision; cell.value is for ordering/calculation only.
Never coerce empty, missing or null cells to zero. Raw layout-only rows are archived, not data rows.
Compare within one table/protocol/split/metric at a time; keep k, language flags and baseline adaptations visible.
No error bars or significance claims: uncertainty statistics and exact metric denominators are unreported.
Do not combine these aggregates into a made-up overall score or a closed-loop success claim.
Do not add remote/internal experiments or reconstructed estimates to the published values.
limitations: ATE and RPE table reporting units are not explicit; do not assume meters from the SR threshold wording.
The test split mixes seen-source and unseen-source trajectories.
LCVN-Uni k=4 uses fewer visual tokens than k=1/2; the context sweep is not a pure fixed-resolution context intervention.
Table 4 is a separate instruction-style experiment; do not overwrite Table 1/2 values with its Concise row.
Table 3 does not report the all-conditioning-off combination. It remains unavailable, not zero.
